appendicitis.name: Appendicitis

answers.pain: It started round my belly button. Now it's moved down here, on the right. Walking makes it worse.
answers.when: Since last night. I thought it was gas, so I had Eno. Twice.
answers.other: I threw up once. Not hungry at all, which is not like me.

appendicitis.exam: Tender low on the right. It hurts more when you let go than when you press.

results.bloods: White count 15,800, raised. The rest is normal.
results.usg: Swollen appendix, 9 mm, with a little fluid around it.

plans.text: Nothing by mouth, a drip, antibiotics and pain relief, and call the surgeons for theatre
plans.why: Classic appendicitis: pain that moved to the right, a fever, a raised white count and a swollen appendix. It needs an operation before it bursts.

plans.text: Antacid and home, come back if it gets worse
plans.why: Pain that moves to the lower right with a fever isn't acidity. Sent home, an appendix can burst.

plans.text: A laxative to clear the bowel and see if it settles
plans.why: Never give a laxative for suspected appendicitis. It can make an inflamed appendix burst.

plans.text: Admit and watch till tomorrow, no antibiotics yet
plans.why: Watching without treatment lets it get worse. Antibiotics and the surgeons, now.

dengue.name: Dengue with warning signs
dengue.board: Fever for four days, now vomiting

answers.pain: Fever, body ache, pain behind my eyes. Today my stomach hurts and I keep vomiting.
answers.when: Four days. The fever's a bit less today, so I thought I was getting better.
answers.other: My gums bled when I brushed this morning. Half our building has fever.

dengue.exam: Tender under the right ribs. Small red spots on the shins. Cool hands.

results.bloods: Platelets 42,000, low. Haematocrit 48%, up since yesterday.

plans.text: Admit, careful drip fluids, paracetamol for the fever, and blood counts every few hours
plans.why: Dengue with warning signs: belly pain, vomiting, bleeding gums, falling platelets and a rising haematocrit. The danger is leaking fluid as the fever settles, so admit and watch closely.

plans.text: Ibuprofen for the fever and the body ache, and home
plans.why: No ibuprofen, aspirin or diclofenac in dengue. They raise the risk of bleeding. And warning signs mean admission.

plans.text: Platelet transfusion straight away, because 42,000 is low
plans.why: Platelets aren't given for a number alone without serious bleeding. Fluids and close watching do the work.

plans.text: Paracetamol and home, the fever's already coming down
plans.why: A falling fever on day four is the most dangerous time in dengue, not the end of it.

renal_colic.name: Kidney stone
renal_colic.board: Back pain going down to the groin

answers.pain: Here, at the back, on the right. It twists and goes down to the front. I can't sit still.
answers.when: It started at four in the morning. It comes in waves.
answers.other: My urine looked a bit pink. No fever.

renal_colic.exam: Restless, can't lie still. Tender over the right side of the back. Belly soft.

results.urine: Blood in the urine. No sign of infection.
results.usg: A 5 mm stone in the right ureter. The right kidney a little swollen.
results.bloods: Kidney function normal. White count normal.

plans.text: A pain-relief injection and an anti-sickness one, then home with tablets, plenty of water and a urology check
plans.why: A small stone, no fever, kidneys working. Most 5 mm stones pass on their own with good pain relief.

plans.text: Book theatre tonight to take the stone out
plans.why: A 5 mm stone without infection usually passes by itself. Surgery tonight isn't needed.

plans.text: Antibiotics and home, no painkillers needed
plans.why: There's no infection, and this is one of the worst pains there is. Pain relief is the treatment.

plans.text: Admit to the ward for a week of drips
plans.why: A week in bed for a small stone helps nobody, and blocks a bed someone else needs.

asthma.name: Severe asthma attack

answers.pain: I can't... get enough air. My chest is tight.
answers.when: Since this evening. They were burning garbage next to our building.
answers.other: I have asthma. My inhaler finished last week. I kept meaning to buy one.

asthma.exam: Wheeze all over the chest. Talking in short bursts. Using the neck muscles to breathe.

results.gas: Oxygen a little low. Carbon dioxide normal for now, which won't last if they tire.
results.xray: No collapsed lung. The lungs are over-inflated.

plans.text: Oxygen, back-to-back salbutamol and ipratropium nebulisers, and steroids, then review in fifteen minutes
plans.why: A bad asthma attack: can't finish sentences, low oxygen, a fast pulse. Nebulisers and steroids now, and watch for tiring.

plans.text: A sedative to calm the panic
plans.why: Never sedate someone in an asthma attack. It slows the breathing they're fighting for.

plans.text: Antibiotics and a cough syrup
plans.why: Nothing here says infection, and syrup won't open airways. The wheeze needs nebulisers.

plans.text: A new inhaler and home
plans.why: Oxygen in the low nineties and broken sentences is a hospital asthma attack, not one for home.

heart_attack.name: Heart attack

answers.pain: In the middle of my chest. Like an elephant sitting on it. It goes into my left arm and my jaw.
answers.when: Forty minutes ago. I was climbing the stairs with the shopping.
answers.other: I have sugar and BP. I stopped the BP tablets, they made me tired.

heart_attack.exam: Grey and sweaty. Chest clear. Heart sounds normal.

results.ecg: ST elevation in II, III and aVF. A heart attack, happening now.

plans.text: Aspirin to chew, the second blood thinner, and call cardiology for the cath lab now
plans.why: Crushing pain, sweating and ST elevation on the ECG: a heart attack in progress. Every minute counts, so open the artery.

plans.text: Antacid and watch, it might be gas
plans.why: Crushing chest pain in a grey, sweaty patient is the heart until proven otherwise. The ECG proved it.

plans.text: Wait for the troponin before doing anything
plans.why: With ST elevation on the ECG you don't wait for blood tests. Heart muscle dies while you wait.

plans.text: A sleeping tablet and a bed on the ward
plans.why: This needs the cath lab, not a ward bed and a sleeping tablet.

dka.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis

answers.pain: My stomach hurts. I've been vomiting since yesterday. I'm so thirsty.
answers.when: Since yesterday. I had a fever and didn't eat, so I didn't take my insulin.
answers.other: I've had diabetes since I was nine. Type one.

dka.exam: Dry mouth. Deep, fast breathing. The breath smells fruity, like nail polish remover.

results.gas: Very acidic: pH 7.12, bicarbonate 9. Ketones high. Potassium 5.6.

plans.text: A fast saline drip first, then an insulin drip, potassium checked every hour, and HDU
plans.why: Diabetic ketoacidosis: high sugar, ketones, acid blood and deep breathing. Fluids first, then insulin, and watch the potassium closely.

plans.text: An insulin injection and home once the sugar falls
plans.why: The sugar is only part of it. The acid and the dehydration take a drip and hours of watching.

plans.text: An anti-sickness injection, and no insulin since they aren't eating
plans.why: Skipping insulin because you're not eating is how DKA starts. Someone with type one diabetes always needs insulin.

plans.text: A bicarbonate drip to fix the acid
plans.why: Bicarbonate isn't the treatment for DKA. Fluids and insulin clear the acid safely.

gastro.name: Food poisoning

answers.pain: Stomach cramps. Loose motions, maybe ten times. And vomiting.
answers.when: Since morning. There was a wedding last night. Paneer, biryani, everything.
answers.other: No blood in it. Three of my cousins have the same thing.

gastro.exam: Dry lips. Belly soft, a little tender all over. Busy bowel sounds.

results.bloods: Sodium and potassium a little low. Kidneys fine.

plans.text: ORS, an anti-sickness injection, a drip till they can drink, then home with advice
plans.why: Food poisoning from the wedding, mild dehydration, no blood. Fluids are the treatment, and most people are better in a day or two.

plans.text: A course of strong antibiotics and admit for a week
plans.why: Watery diarrhoea after a meal is usually a toxin or a virus. Antibiotics don't help and can harm.

plans.text: Nothing by mouth for a day to rest the stomach
plans.why: Starving makes dehydration worse. Small, frequent sips of ORS are the way.

plans.text: Nothing needed, send them home now
plans.why: They're dry and still vomiting. Get fluids in before they go.

viper_bite.name: Viper bite

answers.pain: Here, on my foot. It keeps swelling. My gums are bleeding a little.
answers.when: Two hours ago, in the field. My cousin tied a rope above it and cut it with a blade.
answers.other: It was brown with chain marks on it. My cousin killed it, it's in the bag. You want to see?

viper_bite.exam: Swelling up to the ankle. Oozing from the bite and the cut. Bleeding from the gums.

results.clot: Blood still liquid after 20 minutes. The venom has stopped it clotting.
results.bloods: Platelets low. Clotting times very long.

plans.text: Loosen the rope, keep the leg still, give anti-snake venom, and admit to watch the clotting
plans.why: A viper bite with blood that won't clot. Anti-snake venom is the treatment, and the 20-minute clotting test shows when it's working.

plans.text: Tighten the rope and cut the bite to drain the venom
plans.why: Tight ropes and cutting do harm. They can kill the limb and cause infection and bleeding.

plans.text: Wait and see if it gets worse before giving anti-venom
plans.why: Blood that won't clot is already serious poisoning. Waiting lets bleeding start somewhere worse.

plans.text: Ice on the foot and home, it might be a dry bite
plans.why: The gums are bleeding and the clotting test failed. This is not a dry bite.

wrist_fracture.name: Broken wrist
wrist_fracture.board: Fell on the hand, wrist swollen

answers.pain: My wrist. I slipped in the bathroom and put my hand out.
answers.when: An hour ago. My daughter-in-law brought me.
answers.other: I'm on calcium tablets for my bones. Sometimes I forget them.

wrist_fracture.exam: Swollen wrist, bent like a dinner fork. Fingers pink and moving. Feeling normal.

results.xray: A broken wrist bone just above the joint, tilted backwards.

plans.text: Pain relief, a numbing block, straighten the wrist, a plaster slab and a sling, then the bone clinic
plans.why: A broken wrist that's tilted. Line it up under a block, hold it in plaster, and the bone clinic follows it up.

plans.text: A crepe bandage and home, no X-ray
plans.why: A dinner-fork wrist after a fall is broken until the X-ray says otherwise.

plans.text: Book for surgery tonight
plans.why: Most of these are lined up and plastered in casualty. Surgery isn't the first step tonight.

plans.text: Massage it with oil to bring the swelling down
plans.why: Rubbing a broken bone moves it and hurts. It needs lining up and holding still.

malaria.name: Falciparum malaria

answers.pain: Fever with shivering, then sweating. Headache. It comes back every day.
answers.when: Four days. I came back from a construction site in Odisha last week.
answers.other: The chemist gave me tablets but I can't keep them down. I vomit everything.

malaria.exam: Hot, a little yellow in the eyes. The spleen can be felt under the left ribs.

results.rapid: Malaria rapid test positive for falciparum. Dengue negative.
results.bloods: Parasites on the smear. Platelets low, bilirubin raised. Sugar normal.

plans.text: Admit, artesunate through the drip since they can't keep tablets down, and check the sugar
plans.why: Falciparum malaria, vomiting everything, a little jaundiced. Artesunate through the drip is the treatment, and falciparum can turn severe fast.

plans.text: Chloroquine tablets and home
plans.why: Chloroquine doesn't work against falciparum here, and someone vomiting everything can't take tablets anyway.

plans.text: Antibiotics for typhoid, and paracetamol
plans.why: The rapid test and the smear show malaria. Typhoid tablets treat the wrong disease.

plans.text: Paracetamol and fluids, wait for the fever to break
plans.why: Falciparum doesn't settle by itself. Without artesunate it can reach the brain.

brain_bleed.name: Bleed around the brain

answers.pain: Like someone hit the back of my head with a hammer. The worst headache of my life.
answers.when: It came all at once, an hour ago, while I was lifting a water drum.
answers.other: I vomited twice. The light hurts my eyes. I never get headaches.

brain_bleed.exam: Stiff neck. Screws the eyes up at the light. Drowsy but answering.

results.ct: Blood in the spaces around the brain. A bleed.

plans.text: CT now, then keep the blood pressure down, start nimodipine, and call neurosurgery
plans.why: A sudden worst-ever headache with vomiting and a stiff neck is a bleed around the brain until proven otherwise. The CT proved it.

plans.text: A strong painkiller and home, it's a migraine
plans.why: Migraines build up. A headache that hits like a hammer in seconds is a bleed until the CT says no.

plans.text: A spinal tap first, before any scan
plans.why: With a possible bleed and drowsiness, the scan comes first. A spinal tap is only for when the scan is normal.

plans.text: A bed on the general ward and a recheck in the morning
plans.why: A bleed like this can bleed again within hours. It needs neurosurgery now, not a morning review.

ectopic.name: Burst ectopic pregnancy

answers.pain: Low down, on the right side. Sharp. And now my shoulder hurts, which makes no sense.
answers.when: Since this morning. I nearly fainted in the bathroom.
answers.other: My period is six weeks late. I thought it was stress.

ectopic.exam: Pale. Tender low on the right, tensing against your hand. Cold hands.

results.usg: No pregnancy in the womb. Fluid in the pelvis and a swelling beside the right tube.

plans.text: Two big drips, blood cross-matched, and call gynaecology for theatre now
plans.why: A late period, a positive test, an empty womb and blood in the pelvis: a burst ectopic pregnancy. She's bleeding inside and needs theatre.

plans.text: Urine infection: antibiotics and home
plans.why: Always do a pregnancy test when a woman who could be pregnant has belly pain. Here it was positive.

plans.text: A repeat scan in two days to see where the pregnancy is
plans.why: With low blood pressure and blood in the pelvis there's no time to wait. Waiting can kill.

plans.text: A painkiller and observation on the ward
plans.why: Shoulder pain and fainting mean blood in the belly. It needs theatre, not observation.

pneumonia.name: Pneumonia

answers.pain: Cough. Yellow phlegm. Breathless when I walk to the bathroom.
answers.when: Three days. Today my son says I'm talking nonsense. I'm not.
answers.other: I take tablets for BP. And something for sugar.

pneumonia.exam: Crackles at the bottom of the right lung. Breathing fast. Muddled about the date.

results.xray: A white patch in the lower right lung. Pneumonia.

plans.text: Oxygen, antibiotics through the drip, fluids, and admit
plans.why: Pneumonia in an older person who's confused, breathing fast, with a raised urea. That's a high-risk score: admit and treat through the drip.

plans.text: Cough syrup and home
plans.why: Confusion, fast breathing and low oxygen at this age mean admission, not syrup.

plans.text: Antibiotic tablets and home with the son
plans.why: The right drug in the wrong place. With confusion and low oxygen, this is a hospital pneumonia.

plans.text: Steroids only, for the breathing
plans.why: Steroids don't treat a bacterial pneumonia. Antibiotics do.

chest_wall.name: Strained chest muscle

answers.pain: Here, on the left. Sharp. It hurts when I press it, and when I twist.
answers.when: Since yesterday. I carried two gas cylinders up four floors. The lift was broken, obviously.
answers.other: No sweating, no breathlessness. I googled it, and now I'm scared.

chest_wall.exam: Pressing on the chest wall brings the pain back exactly. Chest clear. Heart sounds normal.

plans.text: Explain it's a strained muscle, paracetamol, and home with a list of reasons to come back
plans.why: Young, pain you can press on and twist into, a normal ECG and troponin. A pulled chest muscle. Reassure, and say clearly when to come back.

plans.text: A clot-busting injection, to be safe
plans.why: Clot-busters cause serious bleeding. They're only for a proven heart attack, and this isn't one.

plans.text: Admit to cardiac care for three days
plans.why: The tests are normal and the story fits a strain. A cardiac bed is for someone else tonight.

plans.text: Home without an ECG, they're young
plans.why: Young people do have heart attacks. Chest pain gets an ECG first, every time.
